newsitem.title: CHINA: China rehearses Deng Xiaoping funeral.
newsitem.headline: China rehearses Deng Xiaoping funeral.

text.p: China on Saturday began rehearsing for the funeral of patriarch Deng Xiaoping, a delicate task for communist leaders attempting to show both respect for the past and confidence for the future.

Television news pictures seen in Hong Kong showed seven uniformed men carrying a casket at an outside site identified as Babaoshan, the Beijing cemetery reserved for China's most senior leaders and communist heroes.
One television station's film of the rehearsal showed a soldier lying inside a glass-covered coffin, apparently simulating China's late paramount leader.
An official at Babaoshan contacted by telephone on Saturday declined to confirm that the rehearsal had taken place, saying only that nothing unusual had occurred there.
Deng died on Wednesday aged 92. In accordance with his wishes, his body will be cremated at Babaoshan and his ashes will be scattered at sea.

The funeral for the man dubbed as "the architect of modern China" will be held on Tuesday at the Great Hall of the People near Beijing's Tiananmen Square. In keeping with communist tradition, no foreign dignitaries will be invited.

The event will mark Beijing's official farewell to a leader whose reforms changed the face of China and the life of every Chinese, and how it is handled is one of the most delicate tasks facing Deng's immediate heirs.
Preparations revealed so far indicate they are planning something very different for Deng than the elaborate funeral of China's last paramount leader, Chairman Mao Zedong, in 1976.
Deng's family, in a letter to the committee of communist party and government elders organising the funeral, has already asked that the body not be displayed to the public.
Instead, Deng's corneas will be donated to an eye bank and parts of his body offered for medical dissection before cremation.

While the funeral ceremony itself is certain to feature careful expressions of dignified grief by top leaders, Beijing has already taken pains to ensure that no unexpected expressions of popular sorrow take place.
At least two citizens who attempted to place floral tributes to Deng at Tiananmen Square on Thursday were hustled away by police, and security around the city centre remains tight.
